div.l: As ye haue herde what nedeth wordes moo
And when this good man sawe that it was so
As he that wise was and obedient
To kepe his forward bi his Fre assent
He seide sithen I shaƚƚ be gynne the game
What welcome be the Cutte a goddis name
Nowe lete vs ryde and herkenyth what I sey
And with that worde we riden forthe on oure wey
And he be gan with right a merye chere
His seide anoone this tale as ye shall here
Whilome there was as an olde storye telleth vs
A duke that hight Thesius ¶ Thesius
Of Thebes he was lorde and goủernoure ¶ Thebes
And in his tyme swiche a conqueroure
That gretter was there noone vnder sonne
Full many a riche contre hadde he wonne
What with his wisdome and his cheualrye
He conquered all the reaume of femenye
That whilome was cleped Sithia ¶ Sithia
And wedded queen ypolita ¶ ypolita
And brought hir home into his contre
With myche glorie and solempnite
And eke hir yonge suster Emelye
And this with victorye and with melodie
Lete I this noble duke to Thebes ryde
And all his hoste in armes hem be side
And serteis if it nere to longe to here
I wolde haue tolde fully the matere
Howe y wonne was the reaume of Femenye
By Thesius and bi his cheualrye
And of the grete batayle for the nones
Be twix Athenes and amyzones ¶ athenes
And howe beseged was ypolita ¶ amyzones
The faire hardy queen of Sithya
And of the feste that was at her weddyng
And of the tempeste at her home cōmmyng
But all thingꝭes I mote as nowe for bere
I haue god wote a large felde to Ere
And weyke ben the oxen in my plough
The remnāunt of my tale is longe ynough
I wil not letten none of this route
Lete eu͗ery felawe telle his tale a boute
And lete se nowe who shall the souper wynne
